outcome: maternal complications (adhesions, postpartum haemorrhage, infections, anaesthetic complications, hysterectomy, maternal deaths)
foetal complications (Apgar score, admission to neonatal unit, neonatal infections, respiratory problems, perinatal death)
cohort: The study included 253 women who underwent caesarean section (CS) deliveries at Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre.
finding: Repeated caesarean section (RCS) deliveries were high and associated with high CS complications, with sepsis being independently associated with RCS.
mod_finding: The overall complication rate was significantly higher in women with repeated caesarean section (67.1%) compared to those having their first CS (32.9%).
